verdict.rationale: Mem0's entity-scoped memory lets developers scope memories by user, agent, app, and session, which supports both private per-user memory and shared/group memory patterns (e.g., an 'app'-scoped memory shared across agents while user-scoped memory stays private). However, there is no explicit documentation of access-control/permission enforcement (e.g., preventing one user/agent from reading another's private memory) — the scoping appears to be a data-partitioning convenience rather than a security boundary. Missing for 10: explicit permission/ACL enforcement docs, multi-tenant isolation guarantees, and independent confirmation that shared vs private scoping actually restricts cross-user access.
